title: Map bookable McDonald's family events near you
summary: Developer Zafer-Liu built a skill that pulls bookable family events from McDonald's official store data and maps them; the author reports 620 bookable sessions across 10 Beijing stores.
agent_role: The agent confirms the city, runs the official query chain from product to session, and generates the map through deterministic scripts. Any booking requires the user to confirm each detail and pay through the official flow.
outcome: The author reports that a 2026-10-09 test found 620 bookable sessions across 10 stores in Beijing. The author also found that the documented tool names differ from the live ones and that session prices are in fen.
what_they_did: Developer Zafer-Liu built a skill in WorkBuddy that answers questions like "what McDonald's events are near me." The agent confirms the city, then uses McDonald's official connector to look up event, city, store, date and session in turn. Small scripts check prices against the store catalog and draw a cartoon map at the stores' official locations. The map shows only sessions confirmed as bookable and can add them to a calendar.
how_it_went: The author reports a live test on 2026-10-09 found 620 bookable sessions across 11 event types at 10 Beijing stores over 14 days.
worth_knowing: The author found the official instructions used different tool names than the live system, and prices came back in fen, hundredths of a yuan. The spots-left number was always 12, possibly a cap rather than a live count.
prompt: Find [type of event, e.g. kids' birthday parties] at [venue or chain] in [your city] over the next [number] days. Use only official sources or tools, and include a session only if the source says it still has spots. Check each price against the official listing and flag any unit you're unsure of. Give me a list grouped by location, with date, time, price and spots left, nearest to [your area] first. Then make a calendar file of the sessions I pick. Don't book anything; if I ask you to book, list every detail and wait for my approval.

curation.rationale: This contest entry includes a real-token test run with specific findings (wrong documented tool names, prices in fen, a constant seat count) and a demo video. The use case is narrow and partly a contest showcase, so it is borderline; the score includes a small daily-life boost.
